Hi Stephanie,

Thanks again for the demo last week. We want to move forward on Dedicated capacity but need clearer numbers: our engineering director asked for per-model GPU memory profiles that account for 1) 8k vs 64k context plans, 2) whether KV cache is pinned per-tenant or shared, and 3) how different quantization choices change the pod sizing (FP16 vs int8 vs FP8-like).

Could Redwood put together a short playbook that maps our three target models (embedding, assistant-llm, summarizer-64k) to: expected GPU type, GPUs/pod, estimated concurrency at 95th pct, and approximate monthly reserved vCPU/GPU cost? We need this to finish the procurement worksheet.

Also: we care about the graceful degradation path — if a pod is full, what model fallbacks / routing changes do you recommend so SLAs stay acceptable?

Best,
Luke

Subject: RE: Sizing playbook for EverScale deal — per-model memory profiles & precision options

Luke — attaching the initial playbook and a compact spreadsheet with assumptions. Quick summary below. See attached evercale_capacity_model_profiles.xlsx for the numbers per-model.

High-level rightsizing recommendations (short):
- Assistant-LLM (general chat, mixed-length): prefer 48GB GPU pods (A10G-class equivalent) when using FP16 for 8k context. For 64k with KV cache kept on-GPU and large KV residency, move to 80–96GB aggregate per model shard (N=2 x 48GB) or a single 80GB GPU pod with KV offload depending on concurrency.
- Summarizer-64k (long-context batch jobs): if tolerating int8 quantization for encoder layers and FP16 for attention, you can reduce GPU memory by ~28% vs full FP16; this enables 2x the effective concurrency per pod for batch workloads. For low-latency single-shot summaries we recommend dedicated smaller pods with aggressive KV prefix caching.
- Embeddings (short context): int8 quantization works well; can run on smaller 24–32GB GPUs with high concurrency.

Precision tradeoffs we modeled (spreadsheet): FP16 baseline, int8 quantized weights (post-training static) gives ~1.6–1.8x memory reduction, FP8-ish mixed schemes (experimental) show 1.9–2.1x memory reduction but require careful QA and may increase tail-latency by 5–12ms on some layers.

Graceful degradation: recommend routing policy that lives on the control plane. If primary dedicated pod reaches 95% GPU resident KV, route lower-priority requests to: 1) a quantized variant (same model, int8), 2) a smaller-context truncation path (fast but shorter context), or 3) fallback to hosted multi-tenant endpoints for best-effort completions. We include templates for these policies in the doc.

Next steps: Marcus and Karthik — can you validate the memory numbers and add a recommended pod-layout visual? Luke — can you confirm expected 95th percentile concurrency for each model (we assumed 12 for assistant, 6 for summarizer during peak batch windows, 40 for embeddings).

Thanks,
Stephanie

Attachments: evercale_capacity_model_profiles.xlsx (xlsx), proposed_pod_layout_v2.pdf (pdf)
From: marcus_lin@redwood.ai

Subject: RE: RE: Sizing playbook for EverScale deal — per-model memory profiles & precision options

Stephanie — reviewed the spreadsheet and added comments (see Drive link in related_links). A few engineering clarifications below: 

- KV cache sizing: for 64k summarizer we modeled 2.2 tokens per byte on average; assuming sticky sessions, per-tenant KV residency grows fast. If EverScale pins KV per-tenant, provision N=2 x 80GB pods and include an autoscale headroom of ~25% on the reserved pool for burst encoding windows.
- Sharding strategy: use model-sharding (tensor-parallel) for FP16/FP8 modes; for int8 we prefer operator-fusion paths to reduce memory overhead. That shifts pod counts slightly (we estimate 1.1x more pods for int8 when using per-request latency SLAs due to additional CPU pre/post-processing).
- Pod suggestion: For this deal I recommend a mixed pool: 12 x 48GB pods (low-latency assistant), 4 x 80GB pods (64k summarizer with KV residency), and a 16 x 32GB pool for embeddings. Reserve one canary pod per pool for safe rollouts.

I tagged the precise GPU SKUs in the spreadsheet. I'll update the pod_layout pdf with network/NUMA notes by Monday.

-Marcus

Thanks — this is very helpful. Asha and I reviewed the spreadsheet and the proposed mixed-pool approach makes sense. A couple of follow-ups before procurement sign-off: 

1) Can Redwood provide an explicit fallback routing policy YAML we can drop into our control plane? If a dedicated pod is saturated, we want deterministic behavior rather than ad-hoc routing.
2) For cost comparison, could you show a delta table: reserved cost (monthly) for the mixed pool vs a single all-48GB pool that scales horizontally? We care about operational complexity vs raw cost.
3) Timeline: procurement wants a 6-week lead time for reserved capacity. If we sign week of Dec 14, when can we expect first production pods live?

If you can get those answers by end of next week we can circulate to procurement and legal.

Luke

On the product side, we can tolerate a small latency increase for quantized tails if it reduces cost materially; we just need the SLA routing paths codified.
